name: Colostrum growth-factor spray

card.summary: Bovine colostrum supplement, including sprays, taken by athletes for its IGF-1 and growth factors to support recovery and lean mass.
card.note: Colostrum samples can carry bacteria; IGF-1 is not absorbed intact.

quick.overview:
Bovine colostrum is the first milk of cows, rich in growth factors including IGF-1 and IGF-2 and in antibodies. Athletes take it as a powder, capsule or spray hoping for faster recovery, better training and more lean muscle.

The chain is recovery and immune support, then more consistent training, then more muscle. One study cited on Wikipedia found 20 g per day over eight weeks of training may raise bone-free lean mass in active adults, while evidence overall is limited and mixed [1].
quick.how: It is taken as a supplement by mouth, with sprays being one product form. Bodybuilding forums have discussed it since the early 2000s, typically alongside training and protein [2][3].
quick.risks: Research suggests many raw colostrum samples carry heavy bacterial loads, with Salmonella detected in 15% of unpasteurised samples; pasteurisation reduces antibody activity [1]. There is no accepted medical use of bovine colostrum for any human condition [1].

lead: Bovine colostrum is the first milk produced by cows after calving. It contains insulin-like growth factors I and II and is sold as a sports supplement in powders, capsules and sprays [1].

Athletes use it hoping to aid recovery, protect against illness during hard training, and support protein synthesis and tissue repair, which could translate into more training and more muscle [1]. IGF-1 itself is not absorbed intact, but some studies suggest supplementation stimulates the body's own IGF-1 production while others do not [1].
Bodybuilding forum discussions date to the early 2000s [2][3][4]. Reviewers describe the research as limited and mixed [1].

chain: Possible support for recovery and immunity
More consistent training, possibly more lean mass
angle.text: Users take colostrum for its growth factors, aiming for better recovery and lean mass. One cited study found a rise in bone-free lean mass in active adults on 20 g/day for eight weeks of training [1].

paras: Athletes take colostrum to try to improve performance, recovery and resistance to illness during intense training [1]. Forum members in 2001-2009 discussed it as a way to raise lean mass, strength and endurance [2][5].

One study found that 20 g/day for eight weeks of exercise training may increase bone-free lean body mass in active adults [1]. In a study of about 30 male runners, a concentrated powder improved one performance test but not another [1]. Evidence is described as limited and mixed, with small studies and variation by dose and collection timing [1].
Many bovine colostrum samples carry high bacterial loads; Salmonella was found in 15% of unpasteurised samples, and pasteurisation inactivates antibodies [1].

Studies in the literature include athletic lean-mass and running studies as well as work on gut permeability, colitis, allergic rhinitis, influenza and wound healing; results are mixed [1]. Wikipedia states there is currently no accepted medical use of bovine colostrum to treat any condition in humans [1].

lore.intro: T Nation threads from 2001 to 2009 discuss colostrum for muscle gain and recovery [2][3][5].

claims.claim: Colostrum increases lean mass and recovery
claims.believers: A forum post says it increases lean muscle, definition, endurance and recovery [5].
claims.experts: One study reports a lean-mass increase at 20 g/day; overall evidence is limited and mixed [1].
